summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with chest pain, shortness of breath, abdominal pain, nausea, and a history of recent UTI and antibiotic use. Evaluation revealed a urinary tract infection caused by ESBL-producing E. coli, which was treated with IV meropenem followed by oral Bactrim. Her pleuritic chest pain was determined to be chronic and not due to pulmonary embolism, despite a history of DVT and subtherapeutic INR. She declined therapeutic anticoagulation bridging and left the hospital against medical advice with an INR of 1.7. Her symptoms of nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea resolved during the stay, with the diarrhea attributed to Levaquin. Chronic issues including HIV, hepatitis B and C, diastolic heart failure, asthma, and obstructive sleep apnea were managed supportively. She was discharged home with a full course of antibiotics, instructions to start Bactrim prophylaxis, and strong recommendations to follow up on anticoagulation and sleep apnea management.
